issue_request: FHIR-32987 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked the Task intent order definition, surfaced through valueset-task-intent.html, to stop saying an order is authorization by a Practitioner because non-practitioners can assign work.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites Git 475d9d07f2, which changed source/request/codesystem-request-intent.xml from "by a Practitioner" to the actor-neutral phrase "authorization for action." Task.intent composes the order code from http://hl7.org/fhir/request-intent, so the shared request CodeSystem was the correct source location.
additional_context: FHIR-21272 is a same-artifact Published/Persuasive issue and later same-line application that refined the wording to "by the requestor", synchronized source/request/request-spreadsheet.xml, and removed the manual Task ValueSet narrative that could have preserved stale definitions.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change was made because source/request/codesystem-request-intent.xml and source/request/request-spreadsheet.xml now say "by the requestor", source/task/valueset-task-intent.xml includes the request-intent code system without a manual narrative override, and no active request/task source still says "by a Practitioner".
